title: Brother, Rest from Sin and Sorrow
description: Brother, Rest from Sin and Sorrow in Tonic Solfa to ALL FOR JESUS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 591 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Burial of a Christian Brother”, where the book credits them to the Bap. Memorial.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ALL FOR JESUS; any other Eights and Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Bro-ther, rest from sin and sor-row; Death is o'er and life is won; On thy slum-ber dawns no mor-row: Rest; thine earth-ly race is run.

lines: Brother, rest from sin and sorrow;
Death is o'er and life is won;
On thy slumber dawns no morrow:
Rest; thine earthly race is run.
Brother, wake; the night is waning;
Endless day is round thee poured;
For the people of the Lord.
Brother, wake; for he who loved thee, —
He who died that thou mightst live, —
Waits thy crown of joy to give.
Fare thee well; though woe is blending
With the tones of earthly love,
Wait thee in the realms above.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ALL FOR JESUS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
